summary: A hands-and-toes hold with knees hovering just off the floor that builds core bracing and shoulder stability.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips, toes tucked.
Brace your core and lift your knees about an inch off the floor.
Keep your back flat and level, like a tabletop.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
cues: Knees an inch off the floor
mistakes: Hips rising higher than the shoulders

summary: A high plank where each knee travels out toward the same-side elbow, training the obliques, abs, and shoulder stability.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands under shoulders and body in a straight line.
Lift one foot and bring the knee out to the side toward the same-side elbow.
Pause briefly while keeping hips low and level.
Return the foot to plank and repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Hips piking up as the knee comes forward
Rushing and losing the plank line

summary: A mountain climber with each knee driving toward the opposite elbow, adding rotation to work the obliques and raise heart rate.
steps: Start in a high plank with shoulders stacked over wrists.
Drive one knee across your body toward the opposite elbow.
Return that foot and drive the other knee across in a quick, alternating rhythm.
Keep the pace steady until the interval ends, then return to plank.
mistakes: Hips bouncing high above the shoulders
Shoulders rocking back behind the hands
Feet barely moving instead of driving the knee

summary: A forearm side plank with controlled hip dips and lifts that strengthens the obliques and the outer hip.
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
Lift your hips into a side plank so your body forms one line.
Lower your bottom hip to lightly tap the floor.
Drive the hip back up high, then repeat and switch sides.
mistakes: Dropping onto the floor instead of tapping

summary: A face-down flutter of opposite arms and legs that strengthens the lower back, glutes, and rear shoulders.
steps: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs long.
Lift your chest, arms, and legs slightly off the floor.
Flutter opposite arm and leg up and down in small, quick alternations.
Lower everything to the floor to finish.
mistakes: Cranking the head up to look forward
Arching hard through the lower back

summary: A reverse tabletop with alternating toe reaches that works the abs and hips while loading the triceps and glutes.
steps: Sit with feet flat and hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing forward.
Lift your hips into a tabletop position.
Kick one leg up and reach the opposite hand to touch the toe.
Return hand and foot to the floor and alternate sides.
mistakes: Bending the kicking knee to meet the hand
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears

summary: A wide-stance squat with toes turned out that strengthens the quads, inner thighs, and glutes.
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulders and toes turned out about 45 degrees.
Brace your core and sit straight down between your heels.
Push your knees out in line with your toes as you lower.
Drive through your feet to stand tall and squeeze the glutes at the top.

summary: Small, continuous pulses in the lower range of a squat that keep the quads and glutes under constant tension.
steps: Stand with feet about shoulder width and lower into a deep squat.
Stay in the bottom third of the squat with weight in your heels.
Pulse up and down a few inches without standing up.
Keep pulsing until the interval ends, then stand up slowly.
mistakes: Rising too high and resting between pulses

summary: A backward lunge that finishes with a knee drive and single-leg balance, building leg strength and stability.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip width apart.
Step one foot back and lower into a lunge until both knees bend near 90 degrees.
Push through the front foot to stand and drive the back knee up to hip height.
Balance briefly at the top, then step back into the next lunge and switch sides.
mistakes: Losing balance and putting the foot down early
Leaning far forward over the front leg

summary: A held glute bridge with alternating foot lifts that challenges the glutes and teaches the pelvis to stay level.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart.
Press through your heels and lift your hips into a high bridge.
Lift one foot a few inches while keeping the hips level.
Set it down and lift the other foot, alternating while the hips stay up.
mistakes: Hips dropping or tilting as a foot lifts
Arching the lower back instead of using the glutes

summary: A short-range bridge with soles together and knees open that isolates the glutes with quick, squeezing reps.
steps: Lie on your back with soles pressed together and knees falling open.
Pull your heels in toward your hips.
Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Lower under control and repeat with short, quick reps.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to get higher
Using momentum instead of the glutes

summary: An all-fours hip raise that lifts a bent knee out to the side, strengthening the glutes and outer hip.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders, knees under hips, and a flat back.
Keeping the knee bent, lift one leg out to the side.
Raise it as high as you can without shifting your hips.
Lower with control, then switch sides.
mistakes: Leaning the torso away to lift higher

summary: A side-lying hip rotation that opens the top knee to strengthen the glutes and outer hip.
steps: Lie on your side with knees bent and hips and feet stacked.
Rest your head on your lower arm and keep your feet together.
Open your top knee as far as you can without rolling the pelvis back.
Close the knee slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Rolling the hips backward to open wider

summary: A push-up from the knees that builds chest, triceps, and shoulder strength with less load than a full push-up.
steps: Kneel and place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and lower your chest to the floor.
Press the floor away to return to straight arms.
mistakes: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides

summary: A push-up with hands on a low step or bench that builds chest and triceps strength on the way to floor push-ups.
steps: Place your hands on a low step or bench, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back until your body is straight like a plank.
Bend your elbows and lower until your chest touches the edge.
Press back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Head dropping ahead of the chest

summary: A push-up that lowers fully to the floor and briefly lifts the hands, enforcing full range for the chest and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands just outside shoulder width.
Lower your whole body until your chest touches the floor.
Lift your hands briefly off the floor, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Replace your hands and press up as one unit to the plank.
mistakes: Lower back sagging when pressing up
Flopping onto the floor without control

summary: A push-up with one hand forward and one back that shifts more load to one side of the chest and triceps.
steps: Set up in a high plank, then move one hand forward and the other back.
Keep your hips square and body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor, then press back up.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Uneven depth or lowering only partway

summary: A push-up followed by alternating shoulder taps that combines chest and triceps work with anti-rotation core control.
steps: Start in a high plank with feet wider than hips for balance.
Perform one push-up with your body in a straight line.
At the top, tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, then replace it.
Tap with the other hand, then begin the next push-up.
mistakes: Hips rocking side to side on the taps

summary: A flow from high plank to downward dog that strengthens the shoulders and stretches the hamstrings and calves.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Push the floor away and send your hips up and back into an inverted V.
Reach your heels toward the floor and press your chest toward your thighs.
Flow forward back into plank with control.
mistakes: Rounding the upper back in downward dog
Sagging hips when returning to plank

summary: A high plank that travels sideways by stepping hands and feet together, building shoulder strength and core control.
steps: Start in a high plank with shoulders over wrists.
Step one hand and the same-side foot out to the side together.
Follow with the other hand and foot to return to a narrow plank.
Take equal steps in each direction.
mistakes: Shoulders drifting away from over the wrists

summary: A face-down arm sweep from hips to overhead that strengthens the upper back, traps, and rear shoulders.
steps: Lie face down with arms by your sides, palms down, forehead near the floor.
Lift your chest and arms slightly off the floor.
Sweep your arms out in a wide arc until they reach overhead, thumbs up.
Sweep back to your hips slowly, keeping the arms off the floor.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher
Letting the arms drop to the floor

summary: A face-down series of Y, T, and W arm raises that strengthens the muscles between and around the shoulder blades.
steps: Lie face down with your forehead resting lightly on the floor.
Lift your arms overhead in a Y shape, thumbs up, then lower.
Lift your arms straight out to the sides in a T, then lower.
Bend your elbows and pull them back into a W, squeezing the shoulder blades, then lower.
mistakes: Lifting the head and chest instead of the arms
Swinging the arms up with momentum

summary: Standing circles with outstretched arms that warm up the shoulders through a gradually larger range.
steps: Stand tall and extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
Make small circles with your arms.
Gradually let the circles grow larger.
Halfway through, reverse the direction.

summary: An inverted V hold that stretches the hamstrings and calves while lengthening the spine and shoulders.
steps: Start on hands and knees with hands slightly ahead of the shoulders.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back into an inverted V.
Press your chest toward your thighs, bending the knees if needed to keep the spine long.
Hold 20–30 seconds, pedaling the heels gently if it feels good.
cues: Bend knees to keep spine long

summary: A kneeling lunge stretch that opens the front of the hip and thigh on the back-knee side.
steps: Kneel and step one foot forward so the front knee is over the ankle.
Tuck your pelvis slightly and shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch.
Reach the arm on the back-knee side overhead.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A deep lunge with the front foot outside the hand that stretches the hips, inner thighs, and glutes.
steps: From a lunge, place both hands inside your front foot.
Lower the back knee if needed and sink your hips low.
Lower onto your forearms if your range allows.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: An all-fours rotation that slides one arm under the body, then opens it to the ceiling to mobilize the upper back.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Slide one arm under your body until that shoulder rests near the floor.
Sweep the same arm up toward the ceiling, turning your chest open.
Move slowly between both positions, then switch sides.
mistakes: Shifting the hips to one side instead of rotating the upper back

summary: A lying stretch with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee that targets the glutes and outer hip.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Hold the back of the bottom thigh and gently pull it toward your chest.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lying twist with the knees dropped to one side that gently rotates the spine and stretches the lower back and glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and arms out to the sides.
Let both knees fall slowly to one side.
Keep both shoulders resting on the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A seated stretch with the soles of the feet together that opens the hips and inner thighs.
steps: Sit tall and press the soles of your feet together, knees falling open.
Hold your feet or ankles and draw your heels comfortably close.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping your back long.
Hold 20–30 seconds.

summary: Controlled standing leg swings front to back and side to side that warm up the hamstrings, hip flexors, and inner thighs.
steps: Stand tall beside a wall or sturdy support and hold on for balance.
Swing one leg forward and back in a controlled arc.
Then swing the same leg side to side across your body.
Grow the range gradually, then switch sides.
mistakes: Swinging wildly beyond a comfortable range
Rocking the torso with each swing

summary: A walking warm-up that pulls one knee to the chest at a time to open the glutes and hips and challenge balance.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip width apart.
Step forward and pull the opposite knee to your chest with both hands.
Rise onto the toes of the standing foot and hold briefly.
Release, step forward, and alternate legs.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the knee

summary: A sit-up that lowers only three quarters of the way down, keeping constant tension on the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet anchored, and hands beside your head.
Curl your spine and flex at the hips to raise your torso toward your knees.
Rise until your torso is roughly upright.
Lower about three quarters of the way down, then begin the next rep before your back touches.
mistakes: Pulling on the head with the hands
Resting flat on the floor between reps

summary: A lying hamstring stretch that starts with hip and knee at 90 degrees and straightens the leg to lengthen the hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back with one leg straight on the floor.
Bend the other hip and knee to 90 degrees, holding behind the thigh if needed.
Slowly straighten the knee toward the ceiling until you feel a stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lying straddle stretch with legs raised that opens the inner thighs using gravity and gentle hand pressure.
steps: Lie on your back with both legs raised toward the ceiling.
Slowly open your legs into a wide V as far as is comfortable.
Rest your hands on your inner thighs and let gravity deepen the stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then bring the legs together slowly.

summary: A lying crunch with alternating elbow-to-knee pedaling that trains the abdominals and obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with lower back pressed down and hands lightly beside your head.
Lift your shoulders into a crunch and raise your knees over your hips, shins parallel to the floor.
Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg.
Switch sides in a slow, pedaling motion.
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands
Moving only the elbows, not the shoulders

summary: A balance-challenging quad stretch on hands and knees that holds one foot behind you to open the thigh and hip flexor.
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Bend one knee and reach back with the opposite hand to hold that foot or ankle.
Keep the knee fully bent and gently press the hip forward toward the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A small side-to-side crunch reaching for each heel that targets the obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and wide, and arms by your sides.
Lift your shoulders a few inches off the floor.
Crunch to one side and touch that heel with the same-side hand.
Return to center and reach to the other heel, alternating.
mistakes: Dropping the head and shoulders between reaches
Pulling the chin into the chest

summary: A side-to-side diagonal bound from one leg to the other that builds lateral power and landing control.
steps: Stand with one foot slightly ahead of the other in an athletic stance.
Push off the front leg and drive the opposite knee forward and up.
Bound diagonally forward to land softly on the other foot.
Absorb the landing and immediately bound diagonally to the other side.
mistakes: Losing balance and stopping between bounds

summary: A standing mobility drill that draws slow circles with the foot to loosen the ankle and calf.
steps: Stand tall and hold a sturdy support for balance.
Lift one foot slightly off the floor.
Draw large, slow circles with your big toe, moving only at the ankle.
Reverse the direction, then switch sides.
mistakes: Moving the whole leg instead of the ankle

summary: A lying figure-four stretch that pulls both legs toward the chest to target the glutes and outer hip.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Place one ankle across the opposite knee.
Grasp the bottom thigh and pull both legs gently toward your chest.
Hold 20–30 seconds, relaxing the neck and shoulders, then switch sides.

summary: A seated stretch with hands behind the head that draws the elbows back to open the chest and front shoulders.
steps: Sit tall on the floor and lace your fingers lightly behind your head.
Draw your elbows back as far as is comfortable.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and keep your chin level.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then relax.

summary: A two-footed jump over a bench or box from a quick countermovement that builds explosive leg power.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder width apart, a bench or box a short distance in front of you.
Dip into a short squat and swing your arms back.
Swing your arms up and jump explosively over the bench.
Land softly with knees bent, turn around, and jump back over.
mistakes: Knees caving inward on takeoff or landing
Choosing a bench too high to clear safely

summary: A lying reverse crunch with bent knees that curls the pelvis off the floor to work the lower abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with arms by your sides and knees bent, feet just off the floor.
Using your abs, draw your knees in toward your chest.
Roll your pelvis back to lift your hips slightly off the floor.
Lower your hips and legs slowly to the start.
mistakes: Swinging the legs to create momentum

summary: A leaning bodyweight triceps extension against a chest-height bar that isolates the triceps.
steps: Grip a sturdy bar at chest height with hands shoulder width apart.
Step your feet back until you lean on straight arms, body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your forehead toward the bar.
Pause, then straighten your elbows to press back to the start.
mistakes: Turning it into a push-up by moving the shoulders

summary: A forearm-plank-to-high-plank press that strengthens the triceps while the core holds the body rigid.
steps: Set up in a forearm plank with forearms shoulder width apart.
Press your palms firmly into the floor.
Straighten your elbows to lift your forearms and rise onto your hands.
Bend your elbows slowly to lower back onto your forearms.
mistakes: Hips rising or sagging during the press
Rocking the hips back to help lift

summary: A row with the legs hooked over a high bar that pulls the body up to train the mid back, lats, and biceps.
steps: Grip a pull-up bar overhand with a medium to wide grip.
Tuck your knees and hook your legs over the bar so you hang below it.
Bend your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades to pull yourself up toward the bar.
Pause briefly, then lower to straight arms.
mistakes: Pulling with the arms only, without retracting the shoulder blades

summary: A forward-traveling lunge that alternates legs with each step, building leg strength and balance.
steps: Stand tall with feet shoulder width apart and hands on your hips.
Step forward and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through your front heel to rise.
Bring the back foot forward into the next lunge, alternating legs.
mistakes: Steps too short, pushing the knee past the toes

summary: A lying leg raise that finishes by lifting the hips toward the ceiling, working the lower abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight and arms at your sides.
Tuck your knees toward your chest.
Extend your legs straight up toward the ceiling.
Curl your pelvis to lift your glutes off the floor, pause, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Using momentum to kick the hips up
Letting the lower back arch on the way down

summary: A forearm plank that lifts the hips toward the ceiling and returns, working the abdominals and shoulders.
steps: Set up in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders.
Squeeze your abs and raise your hips toward the ceiling.
Pause in a high pike position.
Lower your hips slowly back to the plank.
mistakes: Sagging the hips at the bottom
Shifting weight back onto the feet

summary: A standing lean into a wall on the forearms that stretches both calves at once.
steps: Stand facing a wall a couple of feet away.
Lean forward and rest your forearms on the wall.
Keep your heels pressed into the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, stepping closer or farther to adjust the stretch.

summary: A staggered-stance wall lean that stretches the calf of the back leg.
steps: Stand facing a wall with one foot forward and the other back.
Place your hands on the wall and lean forward.
Keep your back heel down and heel, hip, and head in a line.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A quick lateral footwork drill stepping behind with a knee pull that builds agility and hip coordination.
steps: Stand in a relaxed athletic stance with feet a few inches apart.
Quickly step one foot behind the other and pull that knee up.
Drive the arms in rhythm with the knee pulls.
Keep moving sideways, facing forward, then switch directions.
mistakes: Turning the feet and hips to the side

summary: A seated stretch with one leg extended and moved out to the side that targets the hamstrings and inner thighs.
steps: Sit upright near the front of a chair and grip the sides of the seat.
Straighten one knee and pull your toes back toward you.
Move the extended leg out to the side until you feel a stretch.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A seated side bend with one arm overhead that stretches the lats and the side of the lower back.
steps: Sit upright on a chair with feet flat.
Raise one arm overhead and hold the chair with the other hand.
Bend gently toward the side of the holding hand.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A seated stretch gripping the chair back behind you that opens the chest, front shoulders, and biceps.
steps: Sit on the edge of a chair and reach back to grip the chair back.
Straighten your arms and keep your back straight.
Gently move your upper body forward until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Hold 20–30 seconds.

summary: A standing stretch that raises a stick or broom up and behind the head to open the chest and front shoulders.
steps: Stand tall holding a stick or broom in front of you, palms down, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Raise the stick slowly overhead with straight arms.
Ease it back behind your head only as far as is comfortable.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then bring it back down slowly.

summary: A kneeling rest position that sits the hips back onto the heels to gently stretch the back and hips.
steps: Kneel with knees about hip width apart and big toes together.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward or rest them by your feet and lower your forehead to the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly into your back.

summary: A seated neck stretch that gently draws the chin toward the chest to lengthen the back of the neck.
steps: Sit tall and interlace your fingers lightly behind your head.
Let your elbows point forward.
Slowly draw your chin toward your chest using only light hand pressure.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then lift the head slowly.

summary: An explosive push-up that hops the hands sideways each rep, moving around a circle to build upper-body power.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands about shoulder width apart.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Press explosively so your hands leave the floor and shift a short distance to one side.
Land softly with bent elbows and continue around the circle.
mistakes: Jumping too far and losing the plank

summary: A lying crunch that brings knees and arms together over the body to train the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight and arms extended overhead.
Tuck your knees toward your chest and lift your hips slightly.
At the same time, curl your upper body and bring your arms over toward your knees.
Pause, then extend back out slowly.
mistakes: Dropping the legs and arms quickly
Arching the lower back on the return

summary: A crunch that brings one shoulder across toward the opposite knee to train the obliques and abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hands lightly behind your head.
Curl up and bring one shoulder across your body.
At the same time, draw the opposite knee in to meet the elbow.
Lower slowly and repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Pulling the head with the hands
Moving only the elbow, not the shoulder

summary: A reverse lunge with a torso rotation over the front leg that trains the legs and glutes with added core control.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder width apart.
Step one foot back and lower into a reverse lunge.
Rotate your torso across the front leg.
Rotate back to center, return to standing, and alternate sides.
mistakes: Front knee caving as you rotate
Rounding the back during the twist

summary: A crunch with arms extended overhead, which lengthens the lever and increases the challenge for the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms straight overhead with palms crossed.
Keep your arms in line with your head throughout.
Curl up until your shoulder blades lift off the floor.
Lower slowly to the start.
mistakes: Swinging the arms forward to help
Lifting the lower back off the floor

summary: A short-range curl of the upper back off the floor that targets the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Rest your hands lightly beside your head without lacing the fingers.
Press your lower back down and curl your shoulders off the floor.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Pulling on the head and neck

summary: A seated twist with one leg crossed over the other that stretches the lower back, glutes, and outer hip.
steps: Sit tall with one leg straight on the floor.
Cross the other leg over it with the knee bent and foot flat.
Place the opposite arm against the bent knee and the other hand on the floor behind you.
Rotate toward the bent knee and hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A vertical jump that tucks both heels toward the glutes in the air, building leg power.
steps: Stand with knees slightly bent and feet about hip width apart.
Dip quickly into a short squat.
Jump as high as you can and pull both heels up toward your glutes.
Land with knees softly bent to absorb the impact, then repeat.
mistakes: Lifting the knees forward instead of heels back

summary: Standing straight-arm swings to overhead that warm up the lats and shoulders through an increasing range.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder width apart and arms at your sides.
Keeping your arms straight, swing them up in front of you.
Increase the range with each swing until your arms reach overhead.
Lower with control between swings.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top

summary: An exaggerated clapping motion with straight arms that opens the chest and warms up the shoulders.
steps: Stand tall with arms extended straight in front of you, hands together.
Keeping your arms straight, open them back as far as is comfortable.
Bring them back together in front of you.
Gradually increase the speed as you warm up.
mistakes: Arching the lower back as the arms open

summary: Slow circles with the hands on the shoulders that mobilize the shoulder joint and upper back.
steps: Sit or stand tall and place your fingertips on your shoulders.
Raise your elbows to shoulder height, pointing out.
Draw slow, large circles with your elbows.
Reverse direction partway through.

summary: A lying crunch with one leg crossed over that rotates the opposite elbow toward the knee to target the obliques.
steps: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other ankle crossed over it.
Place your hands lightly behind your head.
Curl up and rotate to bring the opposite elbow toward the raised knee.
Lower slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Pulling the head forward with the hands

summary: A standing stretch with hands on the lower back that draws the elbows together to open the chest and front shoulders.
steps: Stand tall with your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Point your elbows out to the sides.
Gently draw your elbows back toward each other.
Hold 20–30 seconds.

summary: Rapid, low skips with minimal air time that build foot speed, rhythm, and conditioning.
steps: Stand relaxed with one foot slightly forward.
Skip with a quick step-hop pattern, alternating legs.
Stay low to the ground and keep contacts short.
Move as quickly as you can while keeping the rhythm.
mistakes: Bounding high instead of staying low

summary: A seated or lying knee tuck from a flat bench or mat that trains the lower abdominals.
steps: Lie on a flat bench or mat with legs extended and hands gripping the sides or under your hips.
Bend your knees and pull your thighs in toward your chest.
Pause briefly with knees near your chest.
Extend your legs slowly back out without letting them drop.
mistakes: Arching the lower back as the legs extend

summary: A lying straight-leg raise to vertical from a flat bench or mat that targets the lower abdominals.
steps: Lie on a flat bench or mat with legs extended and hands gripping the sides or under your hips.
Keeping your legs nearly straight, raise them until they point at the ceiling.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly until your legs are just above level.
mistakes: Arching the lower back as the legs lower
Bending the knees heavily to cheat

summary: A face-down alternating leg flutter off the end of a bench that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Lie face down on a bench with hips at the edge and hold the front of the bench.
Squeeze your glutes and raise your straight legs level with your hips.
Lift one leg slightly higher as the other lowers.
Alternate in a steady fluttering motion, then lower the legs to finish.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher
Letting the legs drop below hip level

summary: A sit-up with soles together and knees open that limits hip flexor help and focuses on the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back, bend your knees, and press the soles together with knees falling open.
Draw your feet in so your legs form a diamond.
Cross your arms over your chest and curl your torso up toward your feet.
Lower slowly to the floor.
mistakes: Using momentum to throw the torso up
Letting the knees lift and close

summary: Straight-leg forward and backward swings beside a support that warm up the hamstrings and hip flexors.
steps: Stand beside a chair or support and hold it with one hand.
Swing the outside leg forward, keeping it straight.
Let it swing down and back as far as your flexibility allows.
Continue in a smooth rhythm, then switch legs.
mistakes: Rounding the back to kick higher

summary: A leaning-back chin-up that pulls the lower chest to the bar, heavily training the lats and upper back.
steps: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Lean back, lift your chest, and arch your upper back.
Pull toward the bar, keeping the lean, until your lower chest touches it.
Squeeze briefly, then lower with control to straight arms.
mistakes: Losing the arch and turning it into a regular chin-up

summary: A kneeling kickback that lifts one bent leg behind you until the thigh lines up with the torso, training the glutes.
steps: Kneel on the floor with hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Keep a soft bend in one knee and lift that leg behind you until the thigh is in line with your back.
Squeeze the glute at the top without arching the lower back.
Lower with control and alternate legs.
cues: Thigh in line with the back
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher

summary: A chin-up combined with a knee tuck that trains the abdominals along with the lats and biceps.
steps: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Bend your knees to 90 degrees.
Pull yourself up while crunching your knees toward your chest until your nose reaches bar height.
Pause, then lower your body and legs slowly to the hang.
mistakes: Letting the legs drop before the body lowers

summary: A seated butterfly stretch that curls forward with elbows inside the thighs to open the groin and lower back.
steps: Sit with knees bent and soles of the feet together.
Rest your hands lightly behind your head.
Curl forward, letting your elbows rest against the inside of your thighs.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then sit back up slowly.

summary: A plank-to-squat jump that brings both feet beside the hands to mobilize the hips and inner thighs.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Jump both feet forward to land beside your hands, keeping your head up.
Pause briefly in the deep squat position.
Jump the feet back to plank and continue.
mistakes: Feet landing well behind the hands
Rounding the back at the bottom

summary: A lying strap-assisted stretch that raises one straight leg to lengthen the hamstrings and calves.
steps: Lie on your back with one leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or towel over the ball of the other foot.
Raise that leg toward the ceiling, keeping the knee straight.
Pull gently on the strap and hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A hanging leg raise that brings straight legs up toward the bar, demanding strong abdominal compression.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, legs together.
Brace your core and draw your shoulders down from your ears.
Raise your legs, piking at the hips, until your feet approach the bar.
Lower slowly to a still hang without swinging.
mistakes: Swinging to get the legs up

summary: An all-fours mobility drill that draws large circles with one bent knee to loosen the hip joint.
steps: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.
Lift one bent knee off the floor.
Draw a large, slow circle with the knee, moving from the hip.
Reverse direction, then switch sides.
mistakes: Shifting the torso to make the circle

summary: A lying stretch that pulls both knees toward the chest to relax the lower back and glutes.
steps: Lie on your back and bring both knees toward your chest.
Hold behind your thighs, under the knees.
Gently draw your knees toward your shoulders.
Hold 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly.

summary: A back extension off the end of a flat bench with a partner holding the legs that strengthens the lower back and glutes.
steps: Lie face down on a flat bench with hips off the end while a partner holds your legs.
Cross your arms over your chest and let your upper body hang down.
Raise your torso until your body is in a straight line.
Lower slowly back down.
mistakes: Rounding the back hard at the bottom

summary: A push-up with hands on an elevated surface that reduces load while building chest, shoulder, and triceps strength.
steps: Place your hands on a bench or sturdy surface slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back until your body and arms are straight.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest to the edge.
Press back up until your arms are straight.

summary: An incline push-up with the hands close together that shifts more of the work onto the triceps.
steps: Place your hands next to each other on a sturdy bar or ledge at a suitable height.
Walk your feet back until your body and arms are straight.
Bend your elbows, keeping them close to your sides, and lower your chest toward your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out to the sides

summary: An incline push-up with a shoulder-width grip that trains the chest, shoulders, and triceps evenly.
steps: Place your hands shoulder width apart on a sturdy bar or ledge.
Walk your feet back until your body and arms are straight.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest to the bar.
Press back up to straight arms.

summary: An incline push-up with palms facing up on a bar that keeps the elbows tucked and adds triceps and upper chest emphasis.
steps: Grip a sturdy bar with palms facing up, hands shoulder width apart.
Walk your feet back until your body and arms are straight.
Bend your elbows, keeping them tucked, and lower your chest to the bar.
Press back up to straight arms.

summary: An incline push-up with hands wider than the shoulders that places more emphasis on the chest.
steps: Place your hands wider than shoulder width on a sturdy bar or ledge.
Walk your feet back until your body and arms are straight.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest to the bar.
Press back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Placing the hands so wide that range is lost

summary: A lying strap-assisted stretch that takes one straight leg out to the side to open the inner thigh and hamstring.
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended and a belt or band looped around one foot.
Raise that leg and let it move out to the side.
Pull gently on the strap until you feel a stretch in the inner thigh.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A face-down strap-assisted stretch that bends the knee and lifts the thigh to open the quads and hip flexors.
steps: Lie face down with a belt or band looped around one foot.
Bend that knee and hold the strap with both hands over your shoulders.
Pull gently so the knee lifts slightly off the floor.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A face-down stretch that reaches one bent leg across the back of the body to open the hip flexors and lower back.
steps: Lie face down with arms out to the sides and palms on the floor.
Bend one knee and reach that leg across behind you toward the opposite hand.
Keep both shoulders on the floor and let the hip open.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A palms-together press in front of the chest that contracts the chest muscles without movement.
steps: Sit or stand tall with elbows bent and palms pressed together in front of your chest.
Point your fingers forward and keep your shoulders down.
Press your hands together, building tension gradually.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then release slowly.

summary: A hand-resisted neck hold that gently pushes the head forward and back against the hands to strengthen the neck.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your head level and facing forward.
Place your hands on your forehead and gently press your head forward without letting it move.
Release slowly, then place your hands behind your head and gently press back.
Hold each direction, breathing steadily, and release the tension slowly.
mistakes: Pushing so hard the head moves

summary: A hand-resisted neck hold that gently presses the head sideways into the hand to strengthen the sides of the neck.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your head level and facing forward.
Place one hand on the same side of your head.
Gently press your head into your hand without letting it move, building tension slowly.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, release slowly, then switch sides.
mistakes: Tilting the head under the pressure

summary: A wide push-up position held with the body shifted toward one bent arm, building chest, shoulder, and triceps strength.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands just outside shoulder width.
Shift your weight toward one hand, bending that elbow to lower your body.
Hold the low, shifted position with the other arm nearly straight.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then press through center and switch sides.

summary: A lying strap-assisted stretch that crosses one straight leg over the body to target the outer hip and glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with a belt or band looped around one foot.
Raise the leg and guide it across your body toward the opposite side.
Keep the leg straight and the foot off the floor, pulling gently on the strap.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then switch sides.

summary: A lying sit-up that raises straight arms and legs to meet over the hips, strongly training the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Exhale and lift your arms, torso, and straight legs at the same time.
Reach your hands toward your shins at the top, balancing on your hips.
Lower your arms and legs slowly back to the floor.

summary: A slow sit-up with glutes and hamstrings tensed that reduces hip flexor involvement to focus on the abdominals.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms crossed over your chest.
Tighten your glutes and hamstrings by pressing your heels into the floor.
Exhale and curl up slowly, keeping that leg tension.
Lower slowly back to the floor.

summary: A ring muscle-up that uses a leg swing to help pull above the rings, training the lats and pushing strength through transition.
steps: Hang from the rings with a false grip, palms over the top of the rings.
Swing your legs back slightly, then drive them forward and up.
Pull hard as the hips rise, bringing the rings toward your armpits.
Roll your shoulders forward over the rings and press up to straight arms.
cues: Pull the rings to the ribs
mistakes: Losing the false grip during the swing
Elbows flaring out at the transition
Pulling too early before the hips rise
